sections.label: Sports Education Programme in schools
sections.summary: The Sports Education Programme is now offered in more than 320 schools, up from 187 five years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: The Sports Education Programme, which promotes development of skills and sports knowledge of students, their active participation of sports, and promotion of team spirit and character building is now offered in more than 320 schools, up from 187 just five years ago.

sections.label: ActiveSG visitorship and weekly participation
sections.summary: Visitorship to ActiveSG facilities rose from 13.2 million in 2014 to about 20.8 million in 2025, with three in four Singaporeans aged 13 and above participating weekly.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: With convenient access to sports programmes at facilities such as gyms and swimming complexes, Singaporeans' visitorship to ActiveSG facilities has increased by more than 50% from 13.2 million in 2014 to about 20.8 million in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Through these efforts, three in four Singaporeans aged 13 and above now participate in sport and fitness activities weekly, up from just one in two a decade ago.

sections.label: Largest SEA Games contingent medals
sections.summary: A contingent of more than 900 athletes across nearly 50 sports won a record 202 medals, with 52 golds.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We fielded our largest SEA Games contingent of more than 900 athletes competing across nearly 50 sports, with more than half competing for the first time.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: They won a record number of 202 medals, with 52 folds.

sections.label: Backstroke personal best relay gold
sections.summary: She set a personal best in the backstroke in the women's 4x100 metres medley relay and, with Ting Wen, Jing Wen and Letitia, broke the meet record and won Gold.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Well, she set her personal best in the backstroke during the womens' 4x100 metres medley relay, and together with her teammates Ting Wen, Jing Wen and Letitia, broke the meet record and won the Gold medal.

sections.label: Team Singapore Paris 2024 medals
sections.summary: The number grew from around 20 in the 2000s to about 40 in the early 2010s to more than 50 today, and at Paris 2024 Team Singapore won two golds, a silver and a bronze.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: From around 20 in the 2000s to about 40 in the early 2010s, to more than 50 today.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: In Paris 2024, our Team Singapore contingent came home with two golds, a silver and a bronze.

sections.label: New home for Team Singapore
sections.summary: A new home for Team Singapore is being invested in as part of the Kallang Alive Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: For our athletes, we are investing in a new home for Team Singapore as part of the Kallang Alive Masterplan.

sections.label: Updating Singapore Sports Council Act
sections.summary: The Singapore Sports Council Act needs updating, having not been significantly updated since its 1973 enactment.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: To support these plans, we need to update the Singapore Sports Council Act, which has not been significantly updated since its enactment in 1973.

sections.label: New section 8(k) mandate
sections.summary: New section 8(k) mandates SportSG to establish an institution consolidating the SSP with the High Performance Sports Institute.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Specifically, new section 8(k) provides SportSG with the mandate to establish an institution formed that will be formed through consolidating the SSP with the High Performance Sports Institute.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: SSP will retain its brand and identity and serve as the educational arm of our HPS system.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: This consolidation will strengthen our system and it will stand us in good stead for future Major Games, especially when we host the SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games in 2029.

sections.label: Defining sports and mind sports
sections.summary: Clause 2 amends section 2 to define sports as including mind sports and e-sports, and mind sport as a competitive intellectual game.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Next, to support Singaporeans' diverse sporting aspirations, clause 2 of the Bill seeks to amend section 2 of the Act to define "sports" to include mind sports and e-sports and to define "mind sport" as a competitive game based on intellectual skill such as chess or bridge.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Clause 6(c) to (f) seeks to amend section 8(f) to (i) to expand the functions in those provisions to include physical fitness activities.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Specifically, cause 6(c) amends section 8(f) to specify that research and study in sports and physical fitness activities includes sports science, sports medicine and other subjects that are related to sports and physical fitness activities.

sections.label: Board size and SportSG powers
sections.summary: Clause 4 increases SportSG's Board maximum from 15 to 25 members, and clause 7 updates SportSG's powers under section 9.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill amends section 4 of the Act to increase the maximum size of SportSG's Board from 15 members to 25 members, so that more expertise could be brought onboard as needed.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Clause 7 of the Bill sets out a detailed list of updates to the powers of SportSG under section 9 of the Act, to align them with the expanded functions of SportSG in section 8 of the Act.

sections.label: Clarity, mandate and flexibility
sections.summary: The proposed amendments give SportSG the clarity, mandate and flexibility to meet these realities responsibly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments give SportSG the clarity, mandate and flexibility to meet these realities responsibly.

sections.label: Formal recognition of SNPC
sections.summary: Formal recognition of the SNPC strengthens accountability, coordination and partnership across the entire sporting ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Athletes with disabilities do not exist on the margins of Team Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, therefore, formal recognition of the SNPC strengthens accountability, coordination and partnership across the entire sporting ecosystem.

sections.label: SportSG promotion powers expanded
sections.summary: The Bill empowers SportSG to promote physical fitness activities, mind sports and e-sports beyond competitive and recreational sport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Beyond competitive and recreational sport, the Bill explicitly empowers SportSG to promote physical fitness activities, mind sports and e-sports.

sections.label: North West Brisk Walking Club
sections.summary: The North West Brisk Walking Club has grown to a membership base of 70,000 spanning seniors, working adults and families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As an example, the North West Brisk Walking Club has grown into, what is perhaps, Singapore's largest and most consistent community fitness movements, with a strong membership base of 70,000 spanning seniors, working adults and families.

sections.label: Standards and SportSG regulation
sections.summary: Standards protect participants, and SportSG does not seek to become a regulator now, with standards not legally binding at this moment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Standards protect not only performance but more importantly the people who participate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I note the assurance that SportSG does not seek to become a regulator at this point in time and that standards will not, at this moment, be legally binding.

sections.label: SSP and HPSI consolidation
sections.summary: Consolidating the SSP and the High Performance Sport Institute into a single entity shifts how athlete development is thought about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The consolidation of the SSP and the High Performance Sport Institute into a single entity represents a significant shift in how we think about our athlete development.

sections.label: SSP relocation to Kallang
sections.summary: The planned relocation of SSP to Kallang alongside national training centres, sports science and sports medicine facilities is promising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The planned relocation of SSP to Kallang, alongside national training centres, sports science and sports medicine facilities, is particularly promising.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill as a statutory foundation for a more inclusive, diverse, professional and humane phase of Singapore sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Sport thrives not by central control but by enabling communities, athletes, volunteers as well as professionals to flourish together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I support this Bill because it provides the right statutory foundation for the next phase of Singapore sports, a phase that is more inclusive, more diverse, more professional and more humane.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The sporting landscape has evolved significantly since the Act was first passed in 1973 and it is only right that our legislative framework reflects modern realities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is a pragmatic step forward to expand the definition of "sport" to include mind sports and e-sports and explicitly incorporate physical fitness activities.

sections.label: Costs of athlete training
sections.summary: Joseph Schooling's parents spent over $1 million on his US training, and Maximilian Maeder estimated about €250,000 yearly for training and competing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To support Joseph Schooling's training in the United States, his parents – Colin and May Yim Schooling – had to spend more than $1 million, including selling a house in Perth and cashing out an endowment plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Maximilian Maeder estimated that the cost of training and competing at his level to be around €250,000 a year.

sections.label: SportSG codes of practice power
sections.summary: New section 8(m) lets SportSG establish and maintain codes, guidelines or standards for sports equipment, items and facilities, creating a potential conflict of interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition, the new section 8(m) will allow SportSG "to establish and maintain codes of practice or conduct, guidelines or standards in relation to any equipment, items and facilities used for sports or physical fitness activities." This creates a potential conflict of interest.

sections.label: Council mandate for sports and fitness
sections.summary: The Bill gives new sports a chance to flourish under the Council's financing and talent development focus, and extends its mandate to physical fitness activities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: By including such new sports under the Council's mandate, the Bill gives them an opportunity to blossom and flourish under a focus on financing and talent development, while allowing them to develop their own frameworks with the Council.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In addition, by extending the Council's mandate to planning and promoting physical fitness activities, the Bill strengthens SportSG's ability to support national priorities, such as preventive health, active ageing and lifelong participation in sport.

sections.label: Career and educational support recognition
sections.summary: The Act's explicit recognition of career and educational support signals that sportspersons' long-term well-being as individuals is valued, not just sporting excellence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The explicit recognition of career and educational support in the Act is an important signal that we value not just sporting excellence, but the long-term well-being of our sportspersons as individuals.

sections.label: Risk-based approach to standards
sections.summary: The speaker seeks the Minister's assurance that the Council would adopt a graduated, risk-based approach with consultation, transition periods and guidance to avoid stifling participation or innovation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Over-regulation or overly rigid standards, if applied too uniformly, may inadvertently increase compliance burdens or even discourage grassroots initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Therefore, may I seek the assurance of the Minister if the Council would adopt a graduated, risk-based approach, with appropriate consultation, transition periods and guidance – so that standards uplift the sector without stifling participation or innovation.

sections.label: Inclusive sports and Bill's purpose
sections.summary: The Bill fortifies the belief that sports should be attainable by all regardless of age, skill or background, and updates the Singapore Sports Council Act to broaden SportSG's mandate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This Bill fortifies the belief that sports should be attainable by all despite age, skill or whatever one's background may be.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I wholeheartedly welcome this effort that brings communities together towards a common ground that fosters sports. : This Bill represents a thoughtful and necessary update to the Singapore Sports Council Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: It equips Sport Singapore with a broader mandate, modern tools and clearer authority to support sport, physical fitness and athlete development in a changing landscape.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I raise my observations and clarifications to ensure that as we expand the scope of sport policy, we do so in a way that remains inclusive, balanced and anchored in the long-term interests of Singaporeans.

sections.label: 2025 Games performance questions
sections.summary: The passage says overall performance at the 2025 Games raises questions about support, infrastructure and strategic direction for athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While our athletes competed admirably, our overall performance at the 2025 Games raises important questions about whether we are providing them with the support, infrastructure and strategic direction they need to succeed.

sections.label: Council expansion concerns
sections.summary: The passage states concerns about expanding the Council from 15 to 25 members under clauses 4 and 5 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This modernises our understanding of competitive excellence and acknowledges that mastery takes many forms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, Mr Deputy Speaker, I have significant concerns about the proposed expansion of the Council from 15 to 25 members, as outlined in clauses 4 and 5 of the Bill.

sections.label: Amendment on Council size
sections.summary: The passage proposes an amendment keeping the maximum Council size at 15 members with expert sub-committees as needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This would provide the specialised expertise needed without bloating the main governing body.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I therefore propose the following amendment that the maximum Council size remains unchanged at 15 members with provisions for establishing expert sub-committees as needed.

sections.label: SportSG institution powers
sections.summary: The passage states clause 6 amends section 8 to grant SportSG powers to establish institutions for developing and training sports persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 6 proposes to amend section 8 to grant SportSG new powers to establish institutions for developing and training sports persons.

sections.label: Support for past athletes
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will extend retroactive support to past athletes who competed before such programmes existed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Having sacrificed their peak earning years and educational opportunities for Singapore's sporting glory, some face financial difficulties, struggle to enter the workforce or lack credentials for career advancement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Will the Government extend retroactive support to these past athletes who competed before such programme existed?

sections.label: CPF for athletes
sections.summary: The passage asks whether additional CPF contributions could be provided for athletes hitting performance targets, including SEA Games representatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Could we provide additional CPF contributions for athletes who hit performance targets, including those who have represented Singapore at SEA Games and other regional competitions?

sections.label: SportSG capability and athlete support
sections.summary: The speaker urges SportSG to show capability on expanded responsibilities, fix past problems, and consider keeping the Council at 15 and supporting past athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Demonstrate that SportSG has the capability on these expanded responsibilities, while also fixing the problems that led to disappointing results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I also urge consideration of the amendments I have proposed: maintain the Council size at 15 and extend meaningful support to past athletes who have already served Singapore.

sections.label: Amendment or suggestion query
sections.summary: The Member asks whether a formal amendment is proposed and cites a record 202 medals: 51 gold, 43 silver, 64 bronze.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Is the Member proposing a formal amendment to the Bill or is he making a suggestion?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: I am not sure by what measure he is referring to, because certainly in terms of medal haul, it was a record of 202 medals: I think 51 gold, 43 silver and 64 bronze.

sections.label: Proposal and SEA Games performance
sections.summary: The speaker says the first point was a proposal and notes that despite broken records, sports like football and badminton did not do well at the 2025 SEA Games.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
sentences.text: So, for the first point that he made, it was a proposal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
sentences.text: And for the second item, with regard to the performance during the 2025 SEA Games, even though we had broken a few records, there are some sports that were not doing well, for example, football and badminton.

sections.label: Singapore fifth in region
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore is still fifth in the region, so there is room for improvement despite exceeding previous medal tallies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik would you like to respond to that clarification of you?

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
sentences.text: So, in general, Singapore in terms of our region, I think we are still fifth, so, I guess there is still room for improvement, even though in terms of medal tally we had exceeded, as compared to previous years.

sections.label: Mountbatten sports hub
sections.summary: Mountbatten hosts national athletes, NSAs, the Singapore National Olympic Council, the Singapore Disability Sports Council and SportSG, and will host the Singapore Sports School under the Kallang Alive Master Plan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Mountbatten is where many of our national sportsmen and sportswomen train, the home base of many NSAs and the Singapore National Olympic Council, the Singapore Disability Sports Council and SportSG itself.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I especially look forward to the realisation of the Kallang Alive Master Plan when the Singapore Sports School will also find a new home in Mountbatten.

sections.label: Expanded sport definition welcomed
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the expanded definition of sport to include e-sports and mind sports, in line with local and international developments.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, I welcome the expanded definition of sport to include e-sports and mind sports, in line with wider local and international developments.

sections.label: Singaporeans exercising regularly proportion
sections.summary: The proportion of Singaporeans who exercise regularly rose from 65% in 2018 to 74% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proportion of Singaporeans who exercise regularly has risen, from 65% in 2018, to 74% in 2024.

sections.label: SportSG discretion over binding standards
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to consider giving SportSG greater discretion to set standards and make them binding beyond ActiveSG-managed facilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would ask the Government to consider whether SportSG should be given greater discretion, not only to set standards but, when necessary, to make them binding across sporting and fitness settings beyond ActiveSG-managed facilities.

sections.label: SportSG approach to developmental programmes
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Government to clarify that SportSG's approach under clause 6(k) is to support a complementary and sustainable ecosystem rather than crowd out or leave programmes to compete.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Government clarify that SportSG's approach under clause 6(k) is not to crowd out these developmental programmes by competing with them, nor to leave them to compete freely over a fixed pool of resources, like previous Members have mentioned, but instead, to support a complementary and sustainable ecosystem?

sections.label: SEA Games gold medal droughts ended
sections.summary: At the SEA Games, hurdler Calvin Quek and diver Avvir Tham each ended longstanding gold medal droughts for Singapore in their events, not seen since Independence in 1965.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More recently and closer to home, at the SEA Games, we witnessed that same inspiration expressed in different ways.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We saw history made as hurdler Calvin Quek and diver Avvir Tham, each ended longstanding gold medal droughts for Singapore in their respective events, achievements not seen since our Independence in 1965.

sections.label: Private donors and SportSG oversight
sections.summary: The speaker suggests engaging the private corporate sector as private donors, notes sport receives the smallest share of charitable donations, and supports the amendment empowering SportSG to oversee the consolidated entity from the SSP and High Performance Sport Institute.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, there is untapped potential in engaging the private corporate sector more deliberately, as some Members have mentioned, but what I would suggest is to engage them as private donors as the commissioner of charities, annual reports consistently show, sport receives the smallest share of charitable donations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this context, I wish to express my strong support for the amendment empowering SportSG to oversee the consolidated entity formed from the SSP and the High Performance Sport Institute.

sections.label: SportSG as integrator of sport
sections.summary: By acting as an integrator aligning education, training and support, SportSG reduces fragmentation, eases burdens on families, strengthens development pathways, and makes high performance sport more accessible to more Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And so, by acting as an integrator – aligning education, training and support, SportSG reduces fragmentation, eases the burden on families and strengthens development pathways; and importantly, this makes high performance sport more accessible to a broader range of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It broadens participation and inclusion, uplift standards and professionalism and sustains high performance sports, so that it inspires us as one united people.

sections.label: Amended sports definition and SportSG role
sections.summary: The Bill updates the statutory definition of sport to include mind sports and e-sports, and expands SportSG's role.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I will speak on three areas: first, the amended definition of sports, second, the expanded role of SportSG; and third, the formal recognition of the Singapore National Paralympic Council, followed by some clarifications for the Ministry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This Bill updates the statutory definition of sport to reflect how participation and competition have evolved, by including mind sports and e-sports.

sections.label: Recognition of Paralympic Council
sections.summary: Formal recognition of the Singapore National Paralympic Council signals that inclusive sport is integral to the national sporting framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Formal recognition of the Singapore National Paralympic Council as a key partner sends a clear signal: inclusive sport is not peripheral, it is integral to our national sporting framework.

sections.label: Council membership increase to 25
sections.summary: The amendment to section 4 raises Council membership to a maximum of 25, up from 15, and seeks the rationale and appointment criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Under the amendment to section 4, membership of the Council will increase to a maximum of 25 members, up from 15, previously.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I seek clarification on the rationale for this increase, as well as the criteria used in appointing Council members.

sections.label: spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarship
sections.summary: The spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarship was introduced, with the inaugural 12 scholars awarded in April 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Next, on athlete support and the spex awards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I note the introduction of the spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarship, with the inaugural 12 scholars awarded in April 2025.

sections.label: SportSG oversight of sports facilities
sections.summary: Under the amendment to section 8, SportSG will oversee management of sports facilities, and a question is raised on booking difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Under the amendment to section 8, SportSG will oversee the management of sports facilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Will it be able to address situations where community organisations or individuals face difficulties booking national facilities, especially at the recently rebranded The Kallang, even when they appear unused for large periods of time?

sections.label: Unused land for short-term sport
sections.summary: The potential of unused open grounds and vacant land being made available for short-term sporting use is raised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: In addition, I would like to raise the potential of unused open grounds and vacant land in the country being made available for short-term sporting use.

sections.label: Accessible sport for all Singaporeans
sections.summary: Sports should be accessible to all Singaporeans, not just a privileged few, so sport can strengthen social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: In order for sports to continue strengthening our social cohesion, we should ensure sport is accessible to all Singaporeans beyond a privileged few, as the hon Dr Hamid has mentioned earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Sports should not be the new measure of affluence.

sections.label: Corporate investment and Paralympic Council
sections.summary: The Member supports more corporate and private sector investment in sporting talents and welcomes the Bill recognising the Singapore National Paralympic Council.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I join several Members who have called for more participation from the corporate or private sectors to invest in our sporting talents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I also welcome the Bill's recognition of the Singapore National Paralympic Council as a key partner of SportSG.

sections.label: Consolidating SSP and Sport Institute
sections.summary: Consolidating the SSP and the High-Performance Sport Institute should enhance end-to-end service delivery across youth and senior athletes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: In particular, the consolidation of the SSP and the High-Performance Sport Institute, should enhance end-to-end service delivery across the youth and senior athlete spectrum.

sections.label: Support for athletes and partnerships
sections.summary: The Member hopes the refreshed Bill brings more inter-Ministry and sector partnerships supporting child athletes, parents and professional women athletes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: E shared with me of her challenges to train competitively, build a family, have a career and seek support to fund her journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am hopeful that the refreshed Bill will see more inter-Ministry partnerships as well as people, private and public sector partnerships to support child athletes and their parents to have an earlier start and discover the pathways designed for the child's success as well as more partnerships so that professional women athletes, too, get the targeted support they need.

sections.label: Support for para-athletes and sporting bodies
sections.summary: Support for para-athletes should expand through coaching, infrastructure and scholarships, with stronger support for sporting bodies and inclusive participation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Additionally, support should be expanded for para-athletes, like Moza Alyka Baihakki who brought glory to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: This includes improving coaching capabilities, ensuring we invest in infrastructure or facilities, and also potentially offering scholarships that provides them with support to further enhance their sporting abilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Government should enhance efforts to ensure stronger support for sporting bodies too so they can fly the Singapore flag high.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: But most importantly, I hope this amendment will result in more people being able to participate in and excel at sport; having a balance in terms of encouragement and support for mind sports and physical sports; as well as providing holistic and constructive education for the development of young athletes, disabled athletes, women, and professional athletes. : Speaker, in gist, the intention of this Bill is to strengthen inclusivity, expand participation and provide better support for athletes of all forms.

sections.label: Record sports participation in Singapore
sections.summary: Sports participation reached an all-time high, with 74% of residents aged 13 and above engaging in sports at least weekly, per the 2022 survey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: More Singaporeans and residents are also participating in sports across different age groups and sports participation in Singapore has reached an all-time high, with 74% of residents aged 13 and above engaging in sports at least once a week, according to the latest National Sports Participation Survey conducted in 2022.

sections.label: SportSG Board size increase
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with the amendment to increase the Board from 15 to 25 members, citing duties of governance, management, accountability and alignment with sporting goals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: As with any Board, its duties include ensuring strong governance, management, accountability and alignment with key sporting goals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I, therefore, agree with the amendment to increase the Board from 15 to 25 members.

sections.label: Singapore's 33rd SEA Games results
sections.summary: Singapore sent 930 athletes across 48 sports to the 33rd SEA Games in Thailand, winning 202 medals: 52 golds, 62 silvers and 89 bronzes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In the recent 33rd SEA Games in Thailand, Singapore sent the largest ever contingent of 930 athletes across 48 sports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: A total of 202 medals were won, namely 52 golds, 62 silvers and 89 bronzes, the biggest medal haul ever.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I was in Thailand, Nonthaburi province to support our table tennis team which contributed four golds, one silver and two bronzes.

sections.label: Julia's swim gold and 2029 SEA Games
sections.summary: Julia set a personal best and helped win the women's 4x100-metre medley gold in a meet record time, and Singapore will host the 35th SEA Games in 2029.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Despite being called on by her coach to replace her injured teammate just 20 minutes before the race, Julia – who had to borrow a swimsuit and a cap – did her personal best and helped the women's swim team win the women's 4x100-metre medley gold in a meet record time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In 2029, Singapore will be hosting the 35th SEA Games and I hope that our whole nation will come together to support, volunteer and cheer for our athletes, coaches and other members of our sports community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The home ground support will give our athletes the extra boost to go the extra mile.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I look forward to the expanded SportSG Board, leading the sporting community towards this milestone SEA Games, rallying the whole of Singapore and bonding Singaporeans through sports.

sections.label: Teenagers' screen time survey
sections.summary: A CNA-Institute of Policy Studies survey found teenagers in Singapore spend more than eight hours a day on electronic devices, with about 60% struggling to reduce screen time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: A CNA-Institute of Policy Studies survey found that teenagers in Singapore spend more than eight hours a day on electronic devices, and about 60% struggle to reduce their screen time.

sections.label: E-sports recognition and screen habits
sections.summary: The speaker asks how official recognition of e-sports will be implemented without normalising unhealthy screen habits, especially for vulnerable youths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: My question to the Ministry is a practical one: how will official recognition of e-sports be implemented in a way that does not normalise unhealthy screen habits, especially for youths who are already vulnerable?

sections.label: Educational and career support for sportspersons
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill's provision for educational and career support for both active and retired sportspersons, citing worries about limited options later on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Others worry about what happens if their child invests heavily in sport but has limited options later on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: That is why I strongly support the Bill's provision for educational and career support for both active and retired sportspersons.

sections.label: Funding for less visible sports
sections.summary: International evidence shows less visible sports, including disability and inclusive sports, tend to receive fewer subsidies unless funding models are deliberately balanced, prompting a question on SportSG's expanding mandate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: International evidence also shows that less visible sports, including disability and inclusive sports, tend to receive fewer subsidies unless funding models are deliberately balanced.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: So, my question is this: as SportSG's mandate expands, how will funding models continue to balance elite performance, grassroots participation and inclusive sport for persons with disabilities, without disadvantaging those with less visibility or commercial appeal?

sections.label: Community sport and coaching standards
sections.summary: The speaker says community sport and grassroots physical activity must keep receiving sustained attention and resources, and supports codes of practice and accreditation for coaching, equipment and facilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: As new categories are brought under its umbrella, it will be important to ensure that community sport and grassroots physical activity continue to receive sustained attention and resources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: I also support the introduction of codes of practice and accreditation for coaching, equipment and facilities.

sections.label: Tiered framework for standards
sections.summary: A tiered framework would apply standards proportionately, with stricter requirements for higher-risk or publicly funded programmes and lighter-touch guidance for grassroots groups, preserving safety and participation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: A tiered framework would allow standards to be applied proportionately, with stricter requirements for higher-risk or publicly funded programmes and lighter-touch guidance for grassroots groups, preserving both safety and participation.

sections.label: Tracking athlete well-being indicators
sections.summary: The speaker says it would be helpful to track well-being, educational progression and post-sport transitions, not just performance outcomes, and notes the Bill gives SportSG greater flexibility and responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: As SportSG oversees these institutions, it would be helpful to track not just performance outcomes, but also well-being, educational progression and post-sport transitions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: These indicators matter if we want to support athletes as people, not just performers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: This Bill gives SportSG greater flexibility – and with it, greater responsibility.

sections.label: Bill updates 1973 Act
sections.summary: The Bill updates a 1973 Act, expanding what is legally recognised as sports to include mind sports and e-sports, extending the Council's remit into physical fitness, and strengthening its ability to uplift standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It updates a 1973 Act so that our national sports agency can reflect the sporting and fitness realities of Singaporeans today.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill does three things: first, it expands what we legally recognise as "sports" to include mind sports and e-sports; second, it extends the Council's remit beyond sport into physical fitness activities; third, it strengthens the Council's ability to uplift standards, through research, coaching guidelines, accreditation and the establishment of training institutions and facilities.

sections.label: Operationalising mind sports recognition
sections.summary: The speaker asks how SportSG will operationalise recognition of mind sports beyond the examples in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My question is: how will SportSG operationalise recognition of mind sports beyond the examples in the Bill?

sections.label: Mind sport recognition framework
sections.summary: Asks whether SportSG should set clearer mind sport recognition criteria, assessment processes and periodic reviews in or under the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If the term "mind sport" becomes too elastic, it may unintentionally undermine the credibility of mind sports as serious competitive pursuits.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Hence, I wonder if it would be good for SportSG to put in place or lay out the following, either in the Bill or when implementing the Bill: a clearer application and recognition framework of mind sports; baseline criteria with inclusions and exclusions more explicitly stated at the outset; a transparent assessment process and a periodic review mechanism of what constitutes as mind sports.

sections.label: Youth e-sports training framework
sections.summary: Asks whether SportSG will develop a structured youth e-sports training framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, will SportSG develop a structured youth e-sports training framework?

sections.label: Parental guidance and consent
sections.summary: Says a national framework could help parents recognise addiction signs and that parental consent should be sought for under-18s in higher-commitment e-sports pathways.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A national framework and research-driven guidance could help parents to understand signs of readiness, set healthy boundaries, recognise warning signs of addiction, such as sleep disruption, mood changes or social withdrawal.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We should also give thought to seek consent from parents whose children are under-18 entering higher-commitment e-sports pathways, so that parents know what is the child enrolling into and can provide the requisite support.

sections.label: Schools and mind sports CCAs
sections.summary: Asks whether there will be joint guidance with MOE on how schools treat and support mind sports CCAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Will there be joint guidance with MOE on how schools should treat and support mind sports CCAs?

sections.label: Fitness activation of unused spaces
sections.summary: Asks whether SportSG will work with HDB, URA and agencies on an assessment framework and pilots for fitness activation of under-utilised spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It depends on proposals coming in one by one, rather than a systematic effort to identify where are the underused or dormant space that can be repurposed for the good of community.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask: with SportSG's expanded mandate, will SportSG also consider working more proactively with HDB, the Urban Redevelopment Authority and relevant agencies to develop a simple, standard assessment framework and a pipeline of pilots for "fitness activation" of suitable under-utilised spaces, such as upper decks of multi-storey car parks?

sections.label: Support for mind sports recognition
sections.summary: Supports recognising mind sports and e-sports because recognition can bring structure, standards and safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In particular, I support the recognition of mind sports and e-sports because it acknowledges that excellence can be achieved cognitively and also physically because recognition can bring structure, standards and safety.

sections.label: Sports access, affordability, quality
sections.summary: He asks about everyday access, affordability and quality of sports facilities, noting commuting is the largest contributor to physical activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Mr, Speaker, Sir, my first clarification concerns everyday access, affordability and the quality of sports facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We often hear that sports participation is at an all-time high, with 74% of residents exercising weekly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, the Ministry of Health's (MOH's) National Population Health Survey reminds us that the largest contributor to physical activity is commuting, not leisure sports.

sections.label: E-sports glamour and risks
sections.summary: He says the glamour of professional e-sports masks that few make it while many risk addiction, sleep disruption and neglected studies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Parents already grapple with excessive screen time, only to be told by their children, "I am not addicted, I am training to go pro." The glamour of professional e-sports masks the truth that only a tiny fraction make it while many risk addiction, sleep disruption and neglected studies.

sections.label: Participation targets for seniors, disabled
sections.summary: He asks whether participation targets can be committed for seniors and persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can we commit to participation targets for seniors and persons with disabilities?

sections.label: Athlete incentives and tracking
sections.summary: He asks if the incentive framework should be reviewed and says graduation rates, post-sport employment and long-term health should be tracked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For many athletes, particularly those who return with medals after years of sacrifice, financial recognition remains limited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I ask the Minister if it is timely to review the incentive framework to better reflect the realities of training at an international level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As SportSG expands its institutional role, we should track graduation rates, post-sport employment and long-term health.

sections.label: Sacrifices of training Singaporeans
sections.summary: He says Singaporeans training while studying, working and supporting families should prompt reflection on whether systems support sustained excellence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Once again, we also saw the immense sacrifices made by Singaporeans who train while studying, working and supporting families, often competing against fulltime athletes from other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Their performances should make us proud but should also prompt us to reflect on whether our systems are truly designed to support sustained excellence.

sections.label: Mind sports and e-sports recognition
sections.summary: He says the Bill's inclusion of mind sports and e-sports signals Singapore recognises competitive excellence wherever it emerges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Chess, bridge and e-sports are no longer just recreational pastimes but are competitive disciplines that demand mental rigour, fill stadiums and attract global audiences in the millions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This Bill's inclusion of mind sports and e-sports in our definition of sports signals that Singapore recognises competitive excellence wherever it emerges.

sections.label: Athlete funding access equality
sections.summary: Asks whether athletes in these disciplines will have the same access to funding, facilities and national representation pathways as athletics or football counterparts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What matters is whether athletes in these disciplines will have the same access to funding, facilities and national representation pathways as their counterparts in athletics or football.

sections.label: E-sports and mind sports scholarships
sections.summary: Asks whether there are plans for e-sports and mind sports athletes to be eligible for Scholarships or High Performance Sport system grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Are there plans for e-sports and mind sports athletes to be eligible for Scholarships or the High Performance Sport system grants?

sections.label: SportSG, MOE, HPB coordination
sections.summary: Asks how SportSG will coordinate with MOE and the Health Promotion Board to avoid duplication or conflicts in fitness education, coaching standards and wellness initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How will SportSG coordinate with MOE and the Health Promotion Board (HPB) to avoid duplication or conflicts in physical fitness education, coaching standards and public wellness initiatives?

sections.label: Investing in sport and athletes
sections.summary: States that supported athletes deserve the country's best, and that investing in sport invests in discipline, character and shared pride.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The athletes we seek to support are giving the best they have to give; whether they compete on a track, a chessboard, or in an arena; therefore, they also deserve nothing less than the best our country can give.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A nation that invests in sport is investing in more than medals – it is investing in discipline, character and shared pride.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As we recognise new forms of competitive excellence, our duty is to ensure that every athlete we support is backed by strong institutions and clear accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When we invest in sport, we invest in the kind of country we want to be.

sections.label: Support for Sports Council Bill
sections.summary: In Mandarin, the Member states support for the Singapore Sports Council (Amendment) Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, I support the Singapore Sports Council (Amendment )Bill.

sections.label: Sport definition includes mind sports
sections.summary: States the amendment updates the definition of sport to include mind sports and e-sports within the statutory scope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, the amendment updates the definition of "sport" to include mind sports and e-sports within the statutory scope.

sections.label: Sports Council physical activities scope
sections.summary: The amendment expands the Sports Council's functions to formally include physical activities within its scope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, the amendment expands the Sports Council's functions to formally include physical activities within its scope.

sections.label: Council standards for coaches facilities
sections.summary: The amendment empowers the Council to establish standards for coaches, facilities and equipment, improving safety and quality of sporting environments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Third, the amendment empowers the Council to establish standards for coaches, facilities and equipment, improving the safety and quality of sporting environments.

sections.label: Bill includes mind sports e-sports
sections.summary: The Bill formally includes mind sports and e-sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Bill formally includes mind sports and e-sports.

sections.label: Expanding Council role physical activity
sections.summary: The Council's role is expanded to include physical activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Two, expanding the Council's role to include physical activity.

sections.label: Council sets coaches facilities standards
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Council to set standards for coaches, facilities and equipment, improving safety and quality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Bill empowers the Council to set standards for coaches, facilities and equipment, improving safety and quality.

sections.label: Support for training providers athletes
sections.summary: The amendments provide clearer institutional support for training providers and smoother pathways for young athletes to develop their potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The amendments provide clearer institutional support for training providers and smoother pathways for young athletes to develop their potential.

sections.label: Bill boosts athlete performance standards
sections.summary: The Bill enhances the system and framework for athletes' performance standards, focusing on four aspects including mind sports, e-sports, sport careers and flexible spaces.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Bill will also enhance our current system and framework to support and boost the performance standards for our athletes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I will focus on four aspects: first, supporting active ageing through mind sports; second, engaging youths through e-sports; third, professionalising sport as a career; and last, expanding flexible sports spaces while managing residents' needs.

sections.label: Formal recognition for e-sports
sections.summary: Formal recognition signals to young Singaporeans that e-sports passions are valued and representing Singapore at the SEA Games and Asian Games is a legitimate national aspiration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Formal recognition matters deeply to young Singaporeans, including those who excel in e-sports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It signals that their passions are valued, that pathways exist for excellence and that representing Singapore at the SEA Games and Asian Games, where e-sports has been a medal event since 2019 and 2023 respectively, is a legitimate national aspiration and not simply a hobby.

sections.label: Merging Sports School and Institute
sections.summary: The Singapore Sports School and High Performance Sport Institute are consolidated into a single entity to enhance end-to-end service delivery across the youth and senior athlete spectrum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Second, the consolidation of Singapore Sports School and the High Performance Sport Institute into a single entity enhances end-to-end service delivery across the youth and senior athlete spectrum.

sections.label: Sports facilities within 10-minute walk
sections.summary: Under the Sports Facilities Master Plan, SportSG aims to provide most Singaporeans with affordable sport facilities within a 10-minute walk of their homes by around 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under the Sports Facilities Master Plan, SportSG aims to provide most Singaporeans with affordable sport facilities within a 10-minute walk of their homes by around 2030.

sections.label: Pickleball noise complaints in HDB estates
sections.summary: The rise of pickleball illustrates tension, with many complaints about pickleball noise in Housing and Development Board estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, the rise of pickleball illustrates the tension vividly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There were many complaints about pickleball noise in Housing and Development Board (HDB) estates.

sections.label: Noise standards and Olympic-sized ice rink
sections.summary: SportSG's mandate to establish codes of practice must include embedded noise management standards, and there is urgency for facilities like an Olympic-sized ice rink.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: SportSG's new mandate to establish codes of practice for equipment and facilities must ensure that embedded noise management standards into facility design and operation are included from the outset.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I would also like to use this opportunity to call out the urgency for other important sports facilities, like an Olympic-sized ice rink, which Singapore has not had for a number of years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our ice hockey and ice-skating athletes have had to go for their trainings in neighbouring countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Not only that, such a facility will encourage more young people to explore their talents in ice sports and provide a fun place for families to enjoy and stay active.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It recognises that sport serves multiple purposes: first, keeping seniors cognitively engaged; second, connecting with youth through formats they find meaningful; third, creating viable career pathways for athletes and coaches; and fourth, providing accessible, flexible facilities in every neighbourhood.

sections.label: spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarships
sections.summary: The passage states support for athletes' aspirations and the launch of spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarships, awarded to an inaugural batch last year.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: And we agree with Members that we should support them to pursue these aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We launched the spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarships and we awarded them to our inaugural batch last year.

sections.label: spexBusiness career support and stipends
sections.summary: spexBusiness partners companies for athlete career support, and spexScholars' monthly stipends were increased with CPF top-ups added.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Through our spexBusiness initiative, we partner a network of supportive companies from diverse industries to provide athletes with career support, flexible workplace practices and development opportunities for their career after sport.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We regularly review and have recently increased our spexScholars' monthly stipends.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: On top of that, they now receive Central Provident Fund (CPF) top-ups, bolstering their finances to better meet their housing, medical and retirement needs.

sections.label: Sports science and entity consolidation
sections.summary: Capabilities in sports science, sports medicine and athlete life management are being deepened, and the Bill consolidates the High Performance Sport Institute and Singapore Sports School.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We are deepening our capabilities in sports science and sports medicine as well as athlete life management, so that we support our athletes holistically, for both their sporting and non-sporting needs and across their life stages.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: And that is also why we are also amending this Bill to allow us to organise ourselves better to serve our athletes, bringing together and streamlining expertise through consolidating the High Performance Sport Institute and Singapore Sports School into a single entity.

sections.label: Athlete accolades and achievements
sections.summary: The passage lists accolades including Trofeo Princesa Sofia Regatta Golds, Formula Kite medals, an Asian Games Gold, and achievements by Amanda Yap and Darren Ong.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: His other accolades include winning Gold thrice at the Trofeo Princesa Sofia Regatta, two Golds and a Silver at the Formula Kite World Championships, and an Asian Games Gold at Hangzhou 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Amanda Yap become Singapore's first-ever gymnast to reach a World Championships Final and placed sixth at the 2025 Artistic Gymnastics World Championship.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: In bowling, Singapore Sports School alumni, Darren Ong, made history as the first male Singaporean bowler to claim the Men's Singles title at the 2023 IBF World Championships since 2006.

sections.label: Consolidation deepens NSA partnerships
sections.summary: Consolidating the High Performance Sport Institute and Singapore Sports School into a single entity will deepen NSA partnerships and provide synergistic, holistic athlete support.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: The consolidation of the High Performance Sport Institute and Singapore Sports School into a single entity will also deepen our partnerships with NSAs and provide synergistic and holistic support to our athletes.

sections.label: Ice rink proposal request
sections.summary: The Singapore Ice Skating Association launched a request for a proposal to develop and operate an ice rink and is reviewing proposals received.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: The Singapore Ice Skating Association has since launched a request for a proposal to develop and operate an ice rink and is reviewing the proposals received.

sections.label: SportSG commercial partners events
sections.summary: SportSG partnered with close to 20 commercial partners for the Singapore Urban Sports and Fitness Festival and over 50 for Olympic Esports Week 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: For example, SportSG partnered with close to 20 commercial partners for last year’s Singapore Urban Sports and Fitness Festival, and over 50 commercial partners for the inaugural Olympic Esports Week in 2023.

sections.label: Support for non-traditional sports
sections.summary: Within land, manpower and funding constraints, support for non-traditional sports comes through the Athletes' Inspire Fund, NSA governance work, event and facility support, and corporate sponsorship.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Within our land, manpower and funding constraints, we have found ways to support non-traditional sports, whether through support for athletes, such as the Athletes’ Inspire Fund, which defrays the costs for athletes in emerging sports participating in regional competitions, or working with NSAs to strengthen governance, obtain charity status and gain access to donations and matching grants to help grow their sports, such as the One Team Singapore Fund, or providing event and facility support, such as to host events like the 2023 World Youth Tchoukball Championship in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: To complement Government funding, we encourage corporates to come in to support our TeamSG athletes.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We have seen some good examples, including Yeo Hiap Seng sponsorship to Max Maeder in 2022 to support his journey towards the 2024 Paris Olympics, and subsequent extension of their sponsorship deal by another four years from 2025 to 2028.

sections.label: Coaches in disability sports
sections.summary: The DSMP targets more than doubling registered coaches who can coach persons with disabilities from 120 to 300 by 2030, alongside raising regular participants from 3,200 to about 5,400.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: One of the strategic moves in the DSMP seeks to enhance the competencies of coaches in disability sports.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We target to more than double the number of registered coaches under the National Registry of Coaches who can coach persons with disabilities, from 120 to 300 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: This will complement other moves to increase the number of regular participants in disability sports programmes from 3,200 today to about 5,400 by 2030.

sections.label: Seniors completing AAC programme
sections.summary: Since September 2024, over 1,200 seniors from 54 AACs have completed the programme.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Since September 2024, over 1,200 seniors from 54 AACs have completed the programme.

sections.label: Inaugural Seniors National Games
sections.summary: The inaugural Seniors National Games saw 4,500 seniors representing 110 AACs compete across five adaptive sports.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: This allows them to continue to reap the benefit of sport, while calibrating the level of physical exertion.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: This culminated in the inaugural Seniors National Games last year, where 4,500 seniors representing 110 AACs competed across five adaptive sports.

sections.label: SportSG equipment conflict of interest
sections.summary: Responding to Mr Fadli Fawzi on clauses 6(m) and 6(l), SportSG typically does not manufacture sports or physical fitness equipment for sale.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Mr Fadli Fawzi asked about a potential conflict of interest SportSG’s expanded function to manufacture and supply sport and physical equipment, as well as to set standards for such equipment in clause 6(m) and 6(l) of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: To clarify, SportSG typically does not manufacture sports or physical fitness equipment for sale.

sections.label: SportSG standards and participation
sections.summary: SportSG says it will stay objective and transparent, and reports higher sports participation and a record SEA Games medal haul.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: SportSG will continue to be objective and transparent as it seeks to uplift industry standards in partnership with our stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We have significantly raised sports participation for Singaporeans from all walks of life – from one in two just a decade ago, to three in four today.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We have made a significant leap in our regional performance, returning from the recent SEA Games in Bangkok with a record haul of medals.

sections.label: Citation year change
sections.summary: The citation year 2025 will be changed to 2026, as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The citation year "2025" will be changed to "2026", as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.
